newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APC says buying Piltel but denies takeover.
newsitem.headline: APC says buying Piltel but denies takeover.

text.p: The APC Group said on Monday its telecom unit Philippine Global Communications Inc (PhilCom) had been buying shares of mobile phone firm Pilipino Telephone Corp (Piltel) from the stock market.
However, APC chairman Jaime Gonzalez dismissed market rumours that international gateway operator PhilCom wanted to take over cellular phone firm Piltel.
PhilCom bought 20 percent of Piltel through a share swap at 20 pesos each last April. Piltel, in turn, has the option to buy 20 percent of PhilCom once it launches an initial public offering.
APC currently owns 40 percent of PhilCom.
"We have bought Piltel shares off the board, because we think it's very much undervalued," Gonzalez said. With the recent stock accumulation, PhilCom owns "slightly more than 20 percent" of Piltel.
"That's probably where we want to be. We are okay with that," he said. However, he hinted that his firm could buy more Piltel shares because of what he said was a cheap price.
Telecom giant Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co owns 30.8 percent of Piltel.
Gonzalez declined to say how much was spent on the buying of the shares, but said it was not PhilCom which drove up Piltel's shares.

Piltel's shares, which had been hit badly by reports of revenue losses from fraudulent calls, fell to an all-time low last week at 9.90 pesos, but recovered steadily to close at 12.50 pesos on Wednesday.
"We haven't bought in the past week," Gonzalez said.
He said Piltel had resolved its problems over the fraudulent calls.
"(April and May numbers) reflect the cleaning up process that's going on there. We're confident that they will more than recover in the succeeding months," he added.
PhilCom recently formed a technical and marketing committee with Piltel to coordinate new fixed-line phone installations in the southern Philippines.
